title: Establish an independent erasure-code corpus
description:
For the one approved code construction, establish reference encoded symbols and recovery cases before implementing the experimental decoder. Cover exact field/code parameters, shortening, padding, metadata, recovery thresholds, duplicate symbols, corrupted inputs and structured burst erasures.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Offline work only after affirmative microfrag.06 scope approval. Do not import restricted code without clearance. The corpus supplies evidence to later implementations; it is neither RF evidence nor permission to modify baseline authentication.
acceptance_criteria: Expected bytes come from published vectors, an independent reference encoder or independently specified finite-field arithmetic, never the production encoder/decoder. Include impossible recovery cases and documented guarantees rather than assuming all equal-sized loss sets are recoverable. Corpus provenance and version are recorded.
